verdict: Trimble grew revenue 7% to $966.8M and hit record recurring revenue of $2.56B, but a much higher tax bill cut GAAP profit nearly in half to $59.1M.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +7% YoY, all of it organic growth

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $0.46 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $0.86

kpis.label: Recurring revenue (ARR)
kpis.note: A record, +11% YoY — the annualized value of subscription contracts

segments.name: Field Systems
segments.note: Surveying, mapping and construction field hardware and software — the largest segment. Segment operating income was $128.7M.

segments.name: AECO
segments.note: Software for architects, engineers, construction and building owners, including the acquired Document Crunch AI platform. Segment operating income was $132.2M.

segments.name: Transportation & Logistics
segments.note: Software for shippers, carriers and supply chains. Segment operating income was $35.7M.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the positioning, modeling and analytics products and subscriptions.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling through dealers, partners and direct channels worldwide.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Restructuring charges, mainly job cuts and cost-saving programs.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of technology and customer relationships bought in past acquisitions.

otherDetail: Non-operating expense of $20.7M, net: $20.4M of interest expense, net, and $1.1M of other losses, partly offset by $0.8M of income from equity method investments.
oneTimers: Restructuring costs were $24.9M in the quarter, and acquisition/divestiture items added $13.1M to operating expenses. Excluding these, amortization and stock-based compensation, non-GAAP EPS was $0.86 versus $0.25 on a GAAP basis.

GAAP results for 2026 so far also include a $562.0M goodwill impairment recorded earlier in the year in the Transportation & Logistics segment. It did not recur in Q3, but it is why full-year GAAP guidance is a loss per share.
footerNote: Trimble's fiscal Q3 2026 ended October 2, 2026. Segment revenue is from the Form 10-Q segment note. Subscription and services were $642.5M of revenue (66%) and product sales $324.3M.

takeaways.title: Recurring revenue hit a record
takeaways.text: Annualized recurring revenue — the annualized value of subscription contracts — reached a record $2.56B, up 11%. Subscription and services brought in $642.5M, two-thirds of all revenue.

takeaways.title: AECO led the growth
takeaways.text: AECO revenue rose 10% to $395.0M and Field Systems rose 7% to $435.8M, while Transportation & Logistics was nearly flat at $136.0M, up 1%.

takeaways.title: A tax spike cut GAAP profit
takeaways.text: The GAAP tax bill was $62.2M — 51.3% of pre-tax profit, versus 10.9% a year ago — after the tax effects of excluded items. GAAP net income fell to $59.1M from $111.5M, while non-GAAP net income was $200.5M.
